road.readiness_formula:
Readiness = (classic rows done + EHR-list features done + department MVPs done) / (classic rows + EHR-list features + department MVPs), with every item weighted 1.

(1) Classic rows. Use the parity doc's own count: Done plus 'Done, with words a recorded decision chose', over the rows not removed (257 today).

(2) EHR-list features. Count the 20 Release A and wave 1 sections plus the 27 Release B, C and P2 sections in EHR_PLANNED_CONTRACT. ORD-13 is left out because the owner decided not to build it, which gives 46. A feature counts as done only when its migrations are signed and on the live backend branch AND the blue screen calls it at real facilities. Backend alone does not count.

(3) Department MVPs. There are 20, counted once each: Appointments (with Patient visits), Referrals, Telemedicine, Inpatient ADT (with wards and ward configuration), ICU, Nursing (with nursing tasks), Maternity, Theatre & Procedures, Radiology, Blood bank, Dental, Patient billing (with the Service catalogue), Insurance & claims (with Policies), Stock & procurement, Reports, Ambulance dispatch (with Vehicles), Shifts/HR & credentials, Quality & safety, Offline wave 1, and the Emergency department board.

Billing and claims count separately because claims are a later, legally gated release. The ED board is added although it was not surveyed. P2-1 to P2-4 are counted in the EHR list, not here.

A department MVP counts as done only when all four hold:
- its MVP scope is served on the live backend;
- every migration is signed verbatim by the owner;
- its required clinical and legal sign-offs are recorded;
- its blue page is live for real facilities, with the sample gone.

Report the three sub-scores beside the headline. Departments are only 20 of 323 items (6.2%), so the headline percentage hides how little of the hospital is built.

deps.mvp_scope: A doctor or clinician sends a referral from a signed visit, and the receiving facility answers it. (1) Send: destination is a Health ID facility listed to receive referrals (directory search, reusing OrderDestinationPicker) or, if the facility is not on Health ID, a printable referral letter recorded as 'printed, outside Health ID'. Required fields: reason, urgency (routine or urgent), specialty or clinic wanted, and the letter text. The sending clinician ticks which current diagnoses, medicines, allergies, recent vitals and released lab results go with it, and the package is frozen when sent. The patient's agreement is clinician-attested, with versioned attestation text as order routes do. There is a respond-by time and withdrawal is allowed before acceptance. (2) Receiving facility 'Incoming referrals' list: accept or decline with a reason. Accepting gives read access to the frozen package only, until completion plus a fixed window. Then mark 'patient arrived', which checks the patient into the waiting list, and finally 'complete with outcome', which sends a short feedback note back to the referring clinician. (3) The referring facility sees the status and the outcome on the visit and on the patient page. (4) The patient sees each referral (destination, status) in the portal and can withdraw it before acceptance, as with ehr.order-route.patient-withdraw. (5) Audit on every send, read and answer, and a support lookup like admin order-routes. Not in the MVP: emergency transfers with ambulance, booking the receiving appointment, full chart access for the receiver, and referrals to individual named consultants. Website work (Lekan): turn the sample's list, new and detail screens and the 'New referral' button into live pages, plus a printable letter and an Incoming tab. Backend: Ola or coordinator agents (cross-facility order routes are her area); Rahman reviews identity and security.
deps.migrations_estimate: 3 (provisional, after the Appointments numbers). First: ehr.referrals and ehr.referral_events plus the frozen package (snapshot rows or a jsonb with references) and SECURITY DEFINER functions to send, withdraw, accept, decline, mark arrived and complete, reusing the order-route attestation texts. Second: a destination listing setting for referrals, a new control key (per the 0086 rule, every control migration must carry all existing keys in its CHECK and in platform.control_enabled), and permissions ehr.referral.send, .receive and .read seeded to doctor and clinician (receptionist only for 'arrived'). Third: the receiving facility's time-limited read of the package (RLS and functions), the counter-referral note, and the patient-portal list and withdraw. Each needs the owner's verbatim signature. It becomes XL if Q-REF-1 B is chosen.
decisions_needed: Q-REF-1 What the receiving facility may read: (A) only the frozen package the sending clinician selected, until completion plus a set number of days; or (B) a time-limited consent grant to the patient's whole chart. Recommend A: NDPA data minimisation, it matches the design's 'Selected clinical summary' and 'Consent scope' fields, and it keeps the size at L.

Q-REF-2 Patient agreement: (A) the clinician attests that the patient agreed, as order routes do ('clinician_attested'), and the patient is told in the portal and can withdraw before acceptance; or (B) the patient must approve each referral in the portal or with their PIN before it is sent. Recommend A, because many referred patients have no portal session at that moment.

Q-REF-3 Destinations: (A) Health ID facilities listed to receive referrals, plus a printable letter for any other facility, recorded as sent outside Health ID; or (B) Health ID facilities only. Recommend A: most Nigerian referrals today are paper letters to facilities that will not be on Health ID at launch.

Q-REF-4 Approval before sending: (A) any doctor or clinician sends directly; or (B) the design's Medical Director 'approve' step first. Recommend A: the backend has no medical director role, and in Nigeria the treating doctor writes the referral letter.

Q-REF-5 On/off control: (A) a new referrals control, seeded off; or (B) reuse cross_facility_orders_enabled, which also switches lab and pharmacy orders. Recommend A, so referrals can be switched on or off without touching lab and pharmacy orders.

Q-REF-6 Urgency scope: (A) MVP offers routine and urgent only, and emergency transfers wait for the Emergency and Dispatch departments; or (B) also allow 'emergency' with a required phone-confirmation field. Recommend A.

deps.mvp_scope: Scheduled remote follow-up consultations for patients the facility already knows. (1) Booking: from Appointments, with mode 'video' or 'phone'. Only clinicians with a recorded MDCN licence attestation may hold sessions. (2) Before the session: the patient gets a portal and inbox notice, and email where available, with a 'Join' button in the signed-in portal. decisions_needed: Q-TEL-1 Video: (A) MVP ships in-browser video through a vetted provider under a DPA, preferring one with in-region (African or EU) processing, with no recording and with audio and phone fallback; or (B) MVP is phone or audio-only remote consultation, documented as a virtual visit, with video added after the DPIA. Q-TEL-2 Recording: (A) never record sessions; or (B) record with the patient's consent and keep the file in the record. Recommend A (smaller NDPA footprint and no media storage).

Q-TEL-4 Who may join: (A) only a patient signed in to the Health ID portal (or their recorded guardian); or (B) also a one-time SMS or email link without sign-in. Recommend A: identity assurance and no link-forwarding risk.

Q-TEL-5 Remote prescribing: (A) allowed as in person, sent through order routes, with controlled medicines blocked; or (B) no prescribing in tele-visits for the MVP. Recommend A, subject to Ola's and the clinical lead's sign-off.
Q-TEL-6 Who may host: (A) only doctors and clinicians with a recorded MDCN licence attestation; or (B) any doctor or clinician role. Recommend A.

deps.mvp_scope: 1) Ward and bed setup per facility. A ward has a name, a type (general, male, female, paediatric, maternity/labour, ICU, private) and its beds. A bed's status is available, occupied, cleaning or maintenance, and a facility can name overflow spaces (for example 'Extra mattress 1'). 2) An admission request from a consultation, the emergency department or the waiting list, carrying the reason, the admitting doctor and the care team. It creates an 'inpatient' encounter, so all existing notes, vitals, orders and prescriptions attach to it. 3) Admit and allocate a bed, enforcing one patient per bed. 4) A bed board and census per ward, showing occupancy, free beds and who is in each bed. 5) Transfer of bed or ward with a nursing handover note, keeping a full movement history. 6) Prepare discharge, then discharge. The outcome is one of routine, against medical advice (DAMA), referred out, absconded or died; died is recorded as an outcome only, with no death certificate. A discharge summary is a signed clinical note with diagnoses, medicines on discharge and follow-up, and it prints. 7) The admission shows on the chart summary and in the patient's access log, and every read and write is audited. Out of the MVP: deposits and bed-day billing, HMO pre-authorisation, bed booking ahead of arrival, offline queueing, death certification.
decisions_needed: Q-ADT-1: What is an admission? A: an 'inpatient' ehr.encounters row plus an admission row that holds the ward, bed and movements, so notes, vitals and orders work unchanged. B: a separate admission record that links to the outpatient visit. Recommend A: it reuses every live clinical route and the existing consent and audit basis.

Q-ADT-2: Who may admit and discharge? A: the doctor or clinician decides the admission and signs the discharge, and nurses allocate and transfer beds. B: nurses may also admit. Recommend A. It matches the design's role mapping (sampleAccess.ts:49: nurse view, create, edit and assign; doctor sign).

Q-ADT-3: How are beds enforced? A: strictly one patient per bed, with named overflow spaces a ward manager can add. B: free-text location, no bed enforcement. Recommend A, because Nigerian wards overflow and named overflow spaces keep the census honest.
Q-ADT-4: Discharge outcomes in the MVP? A: routine, DAMA, referred out, absconded and died (died as an outcome only). B: routine only. Recommend A, with the clinical lead signing the list.

Q-ADT-5: Billing link in the first release? A: ship ADT with no deposit or bed charge; admission never waits on payment. B: wait for point-of-care billing so a deposit can be required. Recommend A. Billing can add a deposit and bed-day lines later, and the defer-for-inpatient rule is already drafted in POINT_OF_CARE_SPEC.

Q-ADT-6: Who sees patient names on the bed board? A: every ward staff member at the facility, as the owner allowed for the waiting list (0135). B: only staff holding that patient's grant. Recommend A, with a DPO check.

Q-ADT-7: Who manages ward configuration? A: facility administrators, through a new ehr.ward.manage permission held by admin and org_admin. B: a new nursing-manager role. Recommend A now, and B later if asked.
Q-ADT-8: Where does it go in the plan? A: a new planned-contract section (Release D, after C). B: fold it into Release C. Recommend A, because Release C is already cut (0147-0149).

deps.mvp_scope: A hospital transfusion service that traces each unit, built inside the lab. (1) Units: record each bag received from the National Blood Service or collected in-house, with unit or donation number, component (whole blood, packed red cells, FFP, platelets), ABO/RhD confirmed by this lab, volume, collection and expiry dates, source, and screening status. The mandatory TTI screens are HIV, HBsAg, HCV and syphilis, each recorded as negative before release; a unit cannot leave quarantine without them. The donor appears only as a donation number, and the donor's identity stays in the facility's existing donor register. (2) Transfusion request: a doctor requests a component and quantity from an encounter, with indication, urgency and the date it is needed. It triggers or links the group-and-screen and crossmatch lab tests. Only the lab-verified group of the patient counts; the self-reported group is never used. (3) Crossmatch and reserve: a lab scientist links a compatible, unexpired unit to the request with its crossmatch result. The system enforces the signed ABO/RhD compatibility table and the crossmatch validity window, and blocks expired, unscreened or incompatible units. (4) Issue: a second person checks and issues the unit. A printed compatibility label and issue slip carry the bag number, the patient's name and Health ID, and both groups. Emergency release of group O units without a crossmatch is allowed with a reason and the doctor's name, and is fully audited. (5) Bedside transfusion record by a nurse: start and end time, pre- and post-transfusion vitals (live vitals), units given, and an adverse reaction with type and severity, which notifies the blood bank and the doctor. (6) Return, expiry and disposal with reasons; a stock view by group, component and expiry; vein-to-vein traceability from unit to patient. Out of MVP: donor registration and donor Health IDs, notifying donors of positive screens, look-back workflows, inter-hospital unit transfer, analyser interfaces, and charging. Suggested owners: Ola (lab owner) for the backend and Rahman for migrations and security; Lekan replaces the sample page.

Add 1 or 2 later for donor management.
decisions_needed: B1. Scope of the first release: A) a hospital transfusion service (units, crossmatch through Lab, reserve, issue, bedside record and reactions) with donors recorded only as donation numbers; B) the same plus full donor management (donor registration, donor Health ID, screening results held against the person, donor notification). Recommendation: A. Donor TTI results (for example a positive HIV screen) are the most sensitive data in the system and need their own DPO and legal review. Do donor management as phase 2.

B2. Compatibility enforcement: A) the system enforces a clinical-lead-signed ABO/RhD compatibility table and a crossmatch validity window, and refuses to reserve or issue otherwise, except a reasoned and audited emergency group O release; B) the system only records what staff decide, like the design's free-text 'Suitability review'. Recommendation: A. Wrong-blood transfusion is a never-event, so the software must stop it.

B3. Which patient blood group counts: A) only a lab-verified group from this facility, with the clinical lead deciding whether a second independent sample is required before the first issue (two-sample rule); B) any recorded group, including the patient-reported one in the health profile (0094). Recommendation: A. The self-reported group must never be used for transfusion.

B4. Where it lives: A) inside the Lab domain (lab-api, the lab role, under the 'laboratory' department, as Akos's design and the 'blood-bank' test category already assume); B) its own service, department code and role.
